method: The Dushanbe Diocese's current fifteenth-anniversary review controls the exact church roster. Current diocesan reports establish additional worship communities visited by its clergy. The official site currently has an expired TLS certificate, so it was read without treating the certificate failure as evidence that the bodies had ceased. Search, maps, and independent directories were used only for discovery.

candidates.name: Saint Luke of Crimea Chapel in Panjikent
candidates.status: hold until a current official report establishes a completed worship building
candidates.reason: The diocese laid the foundation for this chapel in 2018. A 2026 Moscow Patriarchate report still describes a request for land for a future Saint Luke chapel. The current Panjikent community is published, but the unfinished chapel is not represented as a completed church.

candidates.name: Orthodox community in Sarband, now Levakant
candidates.status: hold pending newer current official confirmation
candidates.reason: A December 2022 diocesan report describes a small Russian community and planned recurring clergy visits. No later competent current report was found in this pass.

candidates.name: Orthodox community in Istaravshan
candidates.status: hold pending newer current official confirmation
candidates.reason: The diocese documented this community in 2017, but no newer competent official roster or pastoral report was found in this pass.

reconciliation.result: The diocese's July 2026 review explicitly says seven churches are active in Tajikistan and names all seven. All are published under the Dushanbe Diocese.
The current official report establishes both the community and its local cemetery chapel. They are represented by one combined community row rather than counted twice as separate administrations.

official_jurisdiction_audit.result: Seven active churches and five current worship communities are published. Older or incomplete bodies remain held rather than inferred.

Current official structures of Constantinople, Alexandria, Antioch, Jerusalem, Georgia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria, Poland, the Czech Lands and Slovakia, North Macedonia, ROCOR, the OCA, the UOC, and the OCU were checked for separately administered Tajikistan bodies. No additional exact current body was established by those bounded official structures.

exclusions.result: Discovery listings were reconciled against the competent diocese. They did not establish any additional current canonical worship body independently.
